hints.title: Ordered Tree Split Direction
hints.text: In an ordered tree where every left descendant is strictly smaller and every right descendant is strictly larger, how can the values of p and q direct you toward their split point without searching both sides?

hints.title: Bifurcation Point Invariant
hints.text: If both target values are smaller than the current node, their lowest common ancestor must lie to the left. If both are larger, it lies to the right. If they split on either side, the current node is the answer.

hints.title: Iterative Descent to Split Node
hints.text: Start at the root. While the current node is not null, compare its value with p and q. If both p.val and q.val are strictly less than curr.val, move curr to curr.left. If both are strictly greater, move curr to curr.right. Otherwise, curr is the split node, so return curr.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: H: height of binary search tree (log N balanced, N skewed)
complexity.notes: Follows a single path from root to the lowest common ancestor in O(1) space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generic tree LCA algorithms store node paths or traverse both subtrees, requiring O(N) time and O(N) space regardless of the sorted invariant.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Exploiting the BST ordering property allows a direct iterative descent in O(H) time and strictly O(1) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Direct iterative traversal with O(1) space, identifying the split condition min(p, q) <= curr.val <= max(p, q), handling when p or q is itself the ancestor.
